No. Do not delay emergency action to open a ticket or obtain manager approval [1]. Stop the unsafe activity, move to safety, contact local emergency services when needed, and follow the building’s evacuation instructions [1]. Do not attempt a rescue that creates further danger [1].

Once safe, notify the manager or office coordinator so they can account for affected people [1].

Next step: after reaching safety, make that notification [1].

sources.text:
Request and approval
The manager opens a Service Desk request identifying the person, application, role, reason, and end date where temporary. The system owner approves the role; IT implements it and records evidence. sources.title: Employee Lifecycle and Leave Procedures
sources.text:
Before the start date
People Operations records the signed agreement, start date, manager, work location, and required payroll details in the restricted People Register. The manager opens an onboarding ticket at least three business days before arrival, identifying approved applications, access roles, equipment, and a buddy. IT provisions individual accounts under SEC-05; the manager cannot request a shared login as a shortcut.

sources.title: Company Handbook and Policy Governance
sources.text:
Document change procedure
The owner opens a change entry with the reason, affected documents, proposed wording, and operational impact. Relevant owners review cross-references and thresholds. The COO checks consistency and the CEO approves. The owner publishes the dated version, archives the superseded copy, and assigns training before any new control takes effect. Emergency interim instructions require CEO approval and an expiry within 30 days.

sources.section: 1. Remote work and shared office rules
sources.text:
Equipment and costs
The manager approves necessary equipment through FIN-07. The asset register records custodian, serial number, issue date, and return status. Workers report faults and damage promptly; they must not arrange unauthorized repairs or dispose of equipment themselves.

sources.title: Remote Work, Workplace Safety, and Travel
sources.text:
Reporting procedure
Report a work-related injury, near miss, or significant hazard as soon as safe, normally the same day. Record what happened, location, time, affected activity, and immediate action; avoid speculation about blame. Sensitive medical information goes to People Operations. The office coordinator assigns corrective action and checks completion before reopening an unsafe area.

results.question: May I paste customer data or confidential source code into a public AI tool?
results.answer:
No. Do not place customer data, confidential source code, or personal information into public AI tools or unapproved file-sharing services [1].

Confidential information includes ordinary customer business data [5]. Employees must not store confidential or restricted information in unsanctioned tools [3]. Company confidential information may be used only for authorized work [6].

Approved AI use must follow the specific data permissions recorded for that service, and a person must check outputs before business use [1]. New services require FIN-07 review, including security and privacy checks [1].

Next step: use only an approved service with recorded permissions, or route a new service through FIN-07 review before any such data is entered [1].

Development practices
Keep secrets out of source code, use peer review, scan dependencies, and test with synthetic or de-identified data wherever possible. Production data in a test environment requires the data owner's and Privacy Lead's written approval and equivalent access controls.

sources.title: Acceptable Use and Digital Communications
sources.text: Digital communications must be appropriate to the sensitivity of the information being transmitted. Information classification requirements apply to electronic communications just as they apply to paper records. Employees must avoid sending confidential or restricted information to unapproved recipients or storing it in unsanctioned tools.

sources.title: External Communications and Brand Standards
sources.text: Use of social media and public digital channels must align with this policy and with unacceptable conduct policies. Employees may not publish or repost information that is defamatory, discriminatory, confidential, or otherwise harmful. Personal social media activity may be subject to policy when it relates to the company, impacts the workplace, or reveals company information.

sources.text:
Classification scheme
Public information is approved for external release. Internal information includes routine procedures and nonpublic operating notes. Confidential information includes contracts, nonpublic finances, and ordinary customer business data. Restricted information includes authentication secrets, sensitive personal information, and high-impact customer datasets. The information owner assigns the classification; mixed collections follow the highest applicable level.

results.question: What should I do immediately after losing a company laptop, and should I wipe it myself?
results.answer:
Report the lost laptop immediately. Use the emergency Service Desk channel and notify the IT on-call contact. If that channel is unavailable, call the published internal on-call number [2]. Also report it through the IT help desk or designated security channel [4], and follow SEC-05 and INC-09 [3].

Do not wipe the laptop yourself, investigate independently, or delete evidence [2]. Do not try to recover stolen equipment personally [3]. If you still have a suspected compromised device and it is safe, disconnect it from networks [2].

Secure wiping applies before disposal or reassignment, not as a self-help step after loss [5].

Next: contact the emergency Service Desk and IT on-call now, and do not alter the device.

sources.title: Information Security and Access Management
sources.text:
Device baseline
Company data is handled on managed devices with encryption, screen locking within five minutes, automatic updates, endpoint protection, and remote lock or wipe capability. IT inventories devices and checks compliance before granting access. Personal devices may access only approved low-risk services after an explicit, documented IT review; they may not store Restricted data.

sources.title: Information Security and Access Management
sources.text:
Report and contain
Report a lost device, suspicious login, malware alert, data exposure, or accidental external sharing immediately through the emergency Service Desk channel and notify the IT on-call contact. If that channel is unavailable, call the published internal on-call number. Disconnect a suspected compromised device from networks if safe, but do not wipe it, investigate independently, or delete evidence.

sources.title: Remote Work, Workplace Safety, and Travel
sources.text:
During travel
Carry only the information and equipment needed for the trip. Keep devices with you where practicable, avoid discussing Restricted information in public, and use approved connectivity. Report a lost device immediately under SEC-05 and INC-09. Do not attempt to recover stolen equipment personally. If conditions become unsafe, move to safety and contact the manager when practicable.

results.question: How long are security logs normally kept, and what if they are under an investigation hold?
results.answer:
Security logs are normally retained for 90 days unless they are attached to an incident or hold [1].

If a legal, dispute, or investigation hold applies, deletion of the affected material is suspended until authorized release [5]. Ordinary retention must not delete held evidence [3]. The Privacy Lead or an authorized adviser may impose a hold under DAT-06 [3]. The hold record must include scope, custodian, and the release decision [5].

sources.title: Information Security and Access Management
sources.text:
Records and metrics
Retain access requests and reviews for one year after closure; retain security logs for 90 days unless attached to an incident or hold. Track overdue vulnerabilities, removal timeliness, device compliance, and repeat exceptions monthly. INC-09 governs incident evidence and DAT-06 governs disposal.

sources.title: Privacy, Information Handling, and Records
sources.text:
Customer content and backups
Customer-hosted content follows the signed contract's retention and deletion terms. If terms are absent, the Privacy Lead must resolve them before ingestion. Operational backups follow BCP-10's 35-day rolling window and are not a long-term archive. Deleted material may remain in protected backups until rotation; if restored, required deletions must be reapplied before normal use.

sources.title: Incident Response and Crisis Communication
sources.text:
Evidence preservation
Preserve relevant logs, messages, configuration, timestamps, and original files in restricted storage. Record the collector, source, collection time, transfer history, and any changes made during collection. Do not circulate raw evidence in broad chat rooms. The Privacy Lead or authorized adviser may impose a hold under DAT-06; ordinary retention must not delete held evidence.

sources.title: Code of Conduct and Speak-Up Procedure
sources.text:
Investigation
An uninvolved investigator sets a proportionate scope, interviews relevant people separately, preserves original evidence, and allows the subject a fair opportunity to respond. Interim measures may include reporting-line changes or access restrictions; they are not findings of wrongdoing. People Operations targets completion within 20 business days and provides a progress update at least every ten business days if more time is needed.

sources.title: Privacy, Information Handling, and Records
sources.text:
Overrides and holds
These are illustrative company defaults, not statements of legal minimums. The Privacy Lead records approved jurisdictional or contractual overrides. A legal, dispute, or investigation hold suspends deletion of affected material until authorized release; record scope, custodian, and release decision.

sources.title: Incident Response and Crisis Communication
sources.text:
Communication rules
The communications lead provides a verified internal update at least hourly for SEV1 and every four elapsed hours for SEV2 while active, even if the update is that investigation continues. Support distributes customer updates under SUP-08. The CEO approves public statements; the Privacy Lead coordinates legally or contractually required notices and records applicable deadlines. Approval workflows must not delay a mandatory notice beyond its deadline; escalate immediately to the CEO if timing is at risk.

results.question: What approvals and quotes are required for a $6,000 purchase, and may I split it to avoid the threshold?
results.answer:
A $6,000 purchase is above $5,000, so it needs advance approval from the manager, Finance, and the CEO. Approval is based on total expected value, including taxes, setup, committed renewals, and related purchases. Budget availability does not replace approval, and self-approval is prohibited. [3]

It also requires two comparable quotes, or a documented sole-source justification approved by Finance and the CEO. Evaluate suitability, total cost, security, support, and exit terms, not price alone. Disclose relationships under ETH-02 before participating in selection. [2]

You may not split the purchase to fall below a threshold. [1]

Before ordering or signing, submit the purpose, supplier, total cost, budget code, alternatives considered, delivery needs, and data or system access implications. [1] Only a recorded authorized signatory may sign. Finance issues the purchase reference after approvals. Confirm receipt and record discrepancies before payment. [4]

sources.title: Procurement, Expenses, and Payment Controls
sources.text:
Purchase request
Before ordering or signing, submit the purpose, supplier, total cost, budget code, alternatives considered, delivery needs, and data or system access implications. Do not split a purchase to fall below a threshold. Recurring contracts are assessed on the full committed term; month-to-month services use projected 12-month cost for approval.

sources.text:
Supplier comparison
Purchases above $5,000 require two comparable quotes or a documented sole-source justification approved by Finance and the CEO. Evaluate suitability, total cost, security, support, and exit terms rather than price alone. Disclose relationships under ETH-02 before participating in selection.

sources.title: Procurement, Expenses, and Payment Controls
sources.text:
Approval matrix
All commitments require advance approval based on total expected value, including taxes, setup, renewals committed by the contract, and related purchases. Up to $500 requires manager approval. Above $500 through $5,000 requires manager and Finance approval. Above $5,000 requires manager, Finance, and CEO approval. Self-approval is prohibited; GOV-01 defines substitute approvers. Budget availability is necessary but does not replace approval.

sources.title: Procurement, Expenses, and Payment Controls
sources.text:
Commitment and receipt
Only a recorded authorized signatory may sign a contract. Finance issues the purchase reference after approvals. The requester confirms goods or services were received and records discrepancies before payment. An invoice is not evidence that the purchase was authorized.

sources.title: Procurement, Expenses, and Payment Controls
sources.text:
Reimbursable expenses
Reasonable, necessary business costs are reimbursable when approved and supported. Personal purchases, fines, entertainment unrelated to business, and duplicate claims are not reimbursable. Travel follows WRK-04. Obtain approval against the estimated total before incurring costs; the same FIN-07 thresholds apply to reimbursements.

Reasonable, necessary business costs are reimbursable when approved and supported. Personal purchases, fines, entertainment unrelated to business, and duplicate claims are not reimbursable. Travel follows WRK-04. Obtain approval against the estimated total before incurring costs; the same FIN-07 thresholds apply to reimbursements.

sources.title: Procurement, Expenses, and Payment Controls
sources.text:
Payment verification
Finance matches the approved purchase, receipt confirmation, and invoice, then checks amounts, duplicate invoice numbers, and payment terms. A separate authorized person releases the payment. A worker who changes bank details cannot be the sole verifier or payment releaser.

sources.title: Procurement, Expenses, and Payment Controls
sources.text:
Month-end controls
Finance reconciles bank and card activity monthly, investigates unmatched items, and has an independent reviewer sign off. Track overdue claims, missing approvals, duplicate payments, and supplier concentration. Retain approvals, verification evidence, invoices, claims, and reconciliation records under DAT-06's seven-year financial schedule.

sources.title: Employee Lifecycle and Leave Procedures
sources.text:
Planned departure
People Operations records the final working date and exact access cutoff time, then opens a restricted departure ticket. The manager assigns handover owners, identifies customer commitments, and confirms company property. IT schedules account suspension for the approved cutoff; email forwarding or data transfer requires an identified business purpose and privacy review. Finance handles outstanding expenses and final payments according to applicable requirements.
